goals.title: Reach lunar orbit
goals.summary: Begin in Earth parking orbit, depart with the Saturn upper stage, retrieve Eagle, then brake Columbia and Eagle into lunar orbit.

goals.title: Land Eagle on the Moon
goals.summary: Prepare and undock Eagle, inspect it, lower its orbit and descend. Armstrong and Aldrin land while Collins remains aboard Columbia in lunar orbit.

goals.title: Return the crew to Earth
goals.summary: Launch Eagle's ascent stage, rendezvous with Columbia and return all three astronauts by direct atmospheric entry and Pacific splashdown.

stages.title: Earth parking orbit
stages.controlAuthority: Saturn IU guidance; crew checks and CMC navigation/alignment
stages.description: The spacecraft has reached Earth orbit. Eagle remains inside the closed adapter below Columbia; the S-IVB upper stage is still attached.
stages.historicalAction: Complete insertion and spacecraft checks, perform the CMC P52 platform realignment, and await the Go for TLI.

stages.title: Translunar injection
stages.controlAuthority: LVDC guidance and analog flight control computer; crew monitors the burn
stages.description: The S-IVB restarts its J-2 engine to leave parking orbit on a path toward the Moon. This burn belongs to Saturn's guidance system.
stages.historicalAction: Receive the Go for TLI and monitor stage thrust, guidance and cutoff. Luminary does not command the Saturn engine.

stages.title: Retrieve Eagle
stages.vehicle: Columbia maneuvers to dock with and extract Eagle
stages.computer: Columbia CMC / Comanche 055; crew docking controls
stages.controlAuthority: Collins uses CSM attitude/translation controls; crew operates separation and docking hardware
stages.description: Columbia separates from the upper stage, turns around, docks with Eagle and extracts it. The resulting docked pair continues toward the Moon.
stages.historicalAction: Separate at 003:17:00, dock at 003:24:03 and extract Eagle at 004:16:59; manage probe and vehicle controls with crew oversight.

stages.title: Navigate to the Moon
stages.controlAuthority: Ground tracking and updates, crew navigation observations, CMC guidance and vehicle controls
stages.description: The docked spacecraft coasts toward the Moon. Navigation, spacecraft checks and the required midcourse correction prepare the arrival.
stages.historicalAction: Monitor the trajectory, maintain alignment and spacecraft condition, and perform the required correction using Columbia's propulsion and guidance.

stages.title: Brake into lunar orbit
stages.vehicle: Docked Columbia and Eagle; CSM SPS engine
stages.controlAuthority: CMC-guided SPS burn, enabled and monitored by the crew
stages.description: Columbia fires its service engine on the far side of the Moon, reducing speed enough for lunar capture.
stages.historicalAction: Prepare the SPS maneuver, acknowledge the CMC's flashing Verb 99 with PRO, monitor ignition and select the second valve bank as required.

stages.title: Establish the lunar parking orbit
stages.controlAuthority: CMC-guided SPS maneuver and crew spacecraft management
stages.description: A second SPS burn lowers the high side of the lunar orbit. The crew prepares for the later LM departure.
stages.historicalAction: Complete lunar orbit circularization, verify the orbit, and continue LM checkout and mission preparations.

stages.title: Activate Eagle and prepare guidance
stages.computer: Eagle LGC / Luminary family; separate AGS backup; Columbia CMC
stages.controlAuthority: Crew activation and hardware checks, LM primary guidance and separate abort guidance
stages.description: Armstrong and Aldrin prepare Eagle for independent flight while Collins manages Columbia. Alignment, navigation and target readiness precede descent.
stages.historicalAction: Complete the LM activation and guidance preparations. The linked synthetic P51/P27/P63 experiment demonstrates bounded original-software calculations, not this complete historical activation.

stages.title: Undock and inspect Eagle
stages.vehicle: Eagle and Columbia become separate spacecraft
stages.computer: Separate LGC, AGS and CMC; docking probe is crew-operated hardware
stages.controlAuthority: Collins commands the CSM probe release; LM crew confirms release and manages Eagle
stages.description: Collins releases Eagle from Columbia. The crews manage relative motion and inspect Eagle before the later CSM separation maneuver.
stages.historicalAction: Use the selected, source-backed undocking checklist trainer for crew readiness and EXTD/REL → OFF. Its modeled release does not simulate the full inspection or orbital separation.

stages.title: Lower Eagle's orbit
stages.vehicle: Eagle; Columbia remains in lunar orbit
stages.computer: Eagle LGC / Luminary family; AGS backup
stages.controlAuthority: LM guidance, crew maneuver setup and descent-engine controls
stages.description: After inspection, CSM separation and LM alignment, Eagle fires its descent engine to establish the low point from which powered descent begins.
stages.historicalAction: Verify guidance alignment and the descent-orbit maneuver, perform DOI, and prepare for powered descent. DOI and PDI are separate burns.

stages.title: Descend and land Eagle
stages.computer: Eagle LGC: P63 braking, P64 approach, P66 assisted manual landing
stages.controlAuthority: Original LM guidance/DAP, crew engine and attitude controls, radar feedback and Armstrong's final piloting
stages.description: Eagle brakes, pitches toward the landing area and completes an assisted manual landing. Collins remains aboard Columbia in orbit.
stages.historicalAction: Monitor P63/P64 guidance and alarms, then use the ACA and rate-of-descent controls in P66. The linked propulsion replay is a bounded synthetic fixture, not this flown descent.

stages.title: Tranquility Base
stages.vehicle: Eagle on the Moon; Columbia in lunar orbit
stages.computer: Eagle LGC and AGS; Columbia CMC remains separate
stages.controlAuthority: Crew surface procedures, spacecraft hardware, life support and guidance preparation
stages.description: Armstrong and Aldrin perform the surface mission and prepare to leave. Collins continues the independent Columbia orbital mission.
stages.historicalAction: Secure the descent engine, perform surface operations and ascent preparations. EVA and sample collection are human operations, not AGC commands.

stages.title: Launch from the Moon
stages.vehicle: Eagle ascent stage; descent stage stays on the Moon
stages.computer: Eagle LGC: P12 ascent; AGS backup
stages.controlAuthority: Crew staging/engine preparations and LM ascent guidance; Columbia supports rendezvous
stages.description: Eagle's ascent stage lifts off, leaving its descent stage behind. Armstrong and Aldrin must rendezvous with Collins before returning home.
stages.historicalAction: Prepare the ascent vehicle and P12 guidance, stage and lift off, then verify orbital insertion and prepare the rendezvous maneuvers.

stages.title: Rejoin Columbia
stages.computer: Eagle LGC and AGS; Columbia CMC / Comanche 055
stages.controlAuthority: Rendezvous guidance, crew RCS piloting, docking probe hardware and crew transfer procedures
stages.description: The crews rendezvous and dock. Armstrong, Aldrin and the return cargo transfer to Columbia; Eagle's ascent stage is then jettisoned.
stages.historicalAction: Complete rendezvous, docking and transfer, then discard the LM before the CSM return burn. Eagle does not return to Earth.

stages.title: Depart lunar orbit
stages.vehicle: Columbia Command and Service Modules; all three crew aboard
stages.controlAuthority: CMC-guided SPS maneuver with crew enable, valve selection and monitoring
stages.description: Columbia's service engine accelerates the spacecraft out of lunar orbit and onto the return path.
stages.historicalAction: Prepare TEI, settle propellant, acknowledge the CMC's burn request with PRO, and monitor the SPS maneuver and residual velocity.

stages.title: Navigate home
stages.getLabel: After TEI to ~194:49 GET · historical reference
stages.controlAuthority: Ground tracking, CMC navigation, crew correction and entry preparations
stages.description: Columbia coasts toward Earth's atmospheric entry corridor. Navigation and the required correction prepare the direct return.
stages.historicalAction: Verify the return trajectory, make the required correction, stow equipment and configure the spacecraft for entry. No Earth-orbit insertion burn follows.

stages.title: Enter Earth's atmosphere and splash down
stages.controlAuthority: Crew separation/configuration, CMC entry guidance and RCS, heat shield, parachute/recovery systems
stages.description: The Service Module is discarded before atmospheric entry. Columbia slows in the atmosphere and lands under parachutes in the Pacific Ocean.
stages.historicalAction: Separate the Service Module, orient the heat shield for entry, monitor guidance and deploy/recover under the entry and landing systems. Apollo 11 does not enter a return Earth parking orbit.
